title: Purity and bound energy in ancilla-assisted work extraction
authors: B. Vigneshwar, Farhaan Khan, R. Sankaranarayanan
abstract: We investigate ancilla-assisted work extraction in quantum batteries from the perspective of bound energy and purity. We show that the bound energy of the reduced system provides a tight upper bound to the daemonic gain and that this bound is saturated for globally pure system--ancilla states. Motivated by this relation, we introduce a purity-based gain that qualitatively predicts the daemonic gain without requiring explicit optimization over measurements. We further introduce a protocol to analyze the role of dissipation and intrinsic interactions on daemonic gain. Under a collective environment, dissipation can dynamically generate and stabilize finite daemonic gain through environment-induced correlations. In interacting systems, level crossings and spectral restructuring strongly modify the attainable gain through their influence on the accessible bound energy. Our results demonstrate that daemonic gain is governed not only by correlations, but also by the spectral structure of the underlying Hamiltonian and information loss captured by bound energy and purity.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to understand the maximum extractable work (daemonic gain) from quantum batteries using ancilla assistance. It establishes that this gain is bounded by the system's bound energy and proposes a computationally simpler metric based on global purity ($P_g$). The research further shows how environmental dissipation and intrinsic interactions critically modulate this thermodynamic advantage.
main_problem: The study investigates ancilla-assisted work extraction from quantum batteries by characterizing how bound energy and purity govern the achievable daemonic gain.
main_result: Daemonic gain is governed not only by correlations but also critically by the spectral structure of the Hamiltonian, with a purity-based gain ($P_g$) serving as an effective predictor for this advantage.
method: The authors derive theoretical bounds relating daemonic gain ($\delta W$) to bound energy ($E_b$), and introduce $P_g$ to bypass computationally intensive measurement optimization protocols.
model_or_system: The model involves quantum batteries, treated as bipartite system-ancilla states ($ho_{SA}$), whose dynamics are analyzed under unitary evolution or Lindblad master equations incorporating dissipation.
key_observables: Daemonic Gain ($\delta W$), Bound Energy ($E_b$), Purity-based Gain ($P_g$), Ergotropy ($\xi$).
important_parameters: Dissipation strength ($\gamma_d$), DMI coupling strength ($D$), initial correlation parameters ($\alpha,  eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes the validity of $P_g$ as a proxy for $\delta W$, and later sections analyze specific regimes like weak-DMI or strong-DMI interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate comparisons between $P_g$ and $\delta W$ across pure, mixed, and Werner states; another figure shows the effect of dissipation on gain, and a final set maps $P_g$ dependence on DMI strength ($D$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the upper bound ($\delta W \le E_b$) to introducing the predictive quantity ($P_g$), then analyzing open system dynamics (dissipation), and finally examining how intrinsic interactions modify this gain via spectral restructuring.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium thermodynamics in quantum systems, providing tools to quantify energy harvesting efficiency beyond simple correlation measures by incorporating information theoretic concepts like purity.
